title: Cypress Financial - Procurement MSA/DPA/SLAs Pricing Onboarding

Redwood AE/SE walked through onboarding steps; customer requested SOC2/ISO evidence, updated DPA clauses, and a finalized pricing workbook for approval. Agreed on next steps including MSA redline, security docs, and scheduling a technical onboarding session.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Time: 09:30 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marco Delgado (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Cypress Head of Legal), Liam O'Connor (Procurement), Sarah Nguyen (Infra Lead)

Summary (auto): Procurement kickoff - MSA/DPA/SLAs/pricing and onboarding next steps.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick roundtable, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is priya our se and marco who will help with onboarding and csm stuff.
00:12 Maya Patel: Hi Maya here, head of legal at Cypress. Thanks for setting this up.
00:16 Liam O'Connor: Liam O'Connor, procurement. We'll be shepherding the PO.
00:20 Sarah Nguyen: Sarah, infra. we'll need details on network, VPC peering, egress and KMS stuff.
00:25 Priya Rao: Great, hi all. i'll take the tech questions. quick agenda: MSA redlines, DPA/data residency, SLAs and remedies, pricing numbers and timeline, then onboarding tasks.

03:05 Jordan Lee: Just to frame - we've done the preliminary scoping, we understand cypress wants a private deployment option and reserved capacity maybe, but procurement first wants the contract and security docs. We'll walk through typical redlines and what we can accept.
03:32 Maya Patel: Right - high level from legal: standard carve-outs we ask for, we have some required clauses around data residency and audit rights. Specifically we want the DPA to explicitly state data won't be processed outside EU for EU customer data. Is that something Redwood supports?
03:55 Priya Rao: Yes - Redwood supports region pinning and private deployments. For hosted we have region controls, and for dedicated/private you can run within your VPC. we'll include KMS support for customer-managed keys.
04:22 Maya Patel: Okay, good. We'll need to see the exact DPA language. Also audit rights - we prefer quarterly audit reporting and access to logs.
04:38 Jordan Lee: We can provide SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO certs, and we also provide audit logs export and per-request tracing in the console. Typical ask: we provide the SOC2 and a security whitepaper; for live audits we usually offer a redacted SOC2 or coordinate with our security team.
05:05 Liam O'Connor: On the commercial side, what triggers invoicing and terms? Our procurement needs net-45 payment terms and an invoice sample to route through finance.
05:20 Jordan Lee: We usually do net-30 on self-serve, but for enterprise we can accommodate net-45 at account level; we'll flag that to finance and include an invoice example.
05:32 Marco Delgado: I'll attach a sample invoice and the billing contact flow.

08:10 Sarah Nguyen: On SLAs - Cypress needs 99.95% uptime and a credit structure for downtime. What's Redwood's standard SLA and do you have escalation paths?
08:25 Priya Rao: Our standard enterprise SLA is 99.9%, for dedicated we can go to 99.95 with committed capacity and operational requirements. Remedies: service credits tiered by outage duration. For critical customers we also offer runbook access and a technical account manager.
08:48 Maya Patel: We typically ask for a clawback and liquidated damages for major incidents; is that negotiable?
09:00 Jordan Lee: We can discuss, but full liquidated damages are rare; we can offer higher service credits and an SRE commit during onboarding. We'll surface language that is usually acceptable.

12:15 Maya Patel: About indemnity and liability caps - we need to keep liability in line with services and carve out for data breaches where appropriate.
12:30 Jordan Lee: Our standard liability cap is typically a multiple of fees paid in the preceding 12 months, we can show examples. We can discuss exceptions for willful misconduct.

15:55 Liam O'Connor: Pricing approvals: we have an internal committee that meets weekly. What do you need for them to approve - a final workbook and a sample bill?
16:12 Jordan Lee: Exactly - we'll send a detailed pricing workbook showing committed tier pricing, burst options, and a sample invoice. We'll also include a roadmap for expected token usage and cost per token estimates under different quantization/batching profiles. Priya can include recommended performance/quantization settings for your workload.
16:50 Priya Rao: Right - for your latency-sensitive inference, we recommended dedicated capacity with prefix caching and a 4-GPU pool to hit p95 targets. That will shift unit economics; i'll put numbers in the workbook.

20:00 Maya Patel: For the DPA, we have preferred clause language on subprocessor lists and breach notification timelines (24-48 hours). Can you do 24 hours?
20:16 Priya Rao: Our standard is 48 hours for initial notification and 72 for full report - 24 hours is tough operationally but i'll check with our security ops. We can often commit to an initial ack within 24 hours for critical incidents.
20:35 Maya Patel: Okay please get back on that.

24:10 Jordan Lee: On onboarding - typical steps: 1) finalize MSA/DPA, 2) PO and billing, 3) technical onboarding and SSO/KMS setup, 4) pilot (4 weeks), 5) scale to production. Marco will be CSM.
24:28 Marco Delgado: i'll own onboarding and will coordinate the pilot runbook, checkpoints at week 1 and week 3.

28:00 Sarah Nguyen: Network details - we need VPC peering, or alternatively private link. Also egress firewall rules and ports. Any IP ranges?
28:12 Priya Rao: We'll share network docs; for private deployments we can provide exact CIDR lists and peering guides. For hosted we support AWS PrivateLink and VPC endpoints. KMS integration supports Bring-Your-Own-Key via AWS KMS.

31:40 Maya Patel: We have a couple of redline items in the MSA: change-control for SLAs, data retention terms, and termination assistance. We'll share annotated redlines. What's your preferred format?
31:55 Jordan Lee: Track-changes or a redline PDF is fine. We prefer a single consolidated redline. We'll aim to respond within 3 business days for commercial/legal items and 5 for technical DPA changes but larger legal exceptions may take longer.

36:05 Liam O'Connor: If procurement approves the pricing this week, what's the expected start date for onboarding?
36:15 Marco Delgado: We can start onboarding within 2 weeks of PO and access, and pilot can begin as soon as infra is provisioned - typically 7-10 business days for dedicated pool provisioning if hardware allocation is required.

40:20 Maya Patel: On data residency we need guarantees EU-only processing for EU customer datasets. Will that be reflected in the DPA?
40:30 Priya Rao: Yes, we can include region pinning clauses and show how private deployment keeps data in-customer VPC. We'll include a statement in DPA and supporting runbooks.

44:05 Jordan Lee: Let's recap next steps - i'll send the MSA and pricing workbook; priya will share SOC2 and network/KMS docs; marco will send sample invoice and onboarding checklist. cypress will send back redlines and a list of required DPA clauses.
44:30 Maya Patel: Sounds good. One small ask - can you provide a brief note on SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping? We need to show it to our identity team.
44:40 Priya Rao: Yes, i'll attach an SSO quickstart and RBAC mapping example.

48:00 Liam O'Connor: Procurement timeline - we'll aim to have approvals and PO by 2026-11-25, assuming nothing major in the redlines.
48:12 Jordan Lee: Great, we'll align to that.

50:00 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the artifacts by Friday.
50:06 Maya Patel: Thanks.
50:08 Sarah Nguyen: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker timing offsets and mis-heard words; attendees occasionally overlap.
